summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, chronic diastolic heart failure, and seizure disorder was admitted for periumbilical abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. He presented with hyperkalemia, which was treated successfully. Abdominal CT was unremarkable, and pain resolved after hemodialysis. He developed transient hypoxemia post-dialysis, prompting concern for infection, but imaging and blood cultures were negative. A chest CT showed no acute process, and oxygen needs resolved. A new hepatic lesion was noted on imaging, requiring outpatient follow-up. The patient remained stable, afebrile, and was discharged home on his prior medications with the addition of daily aspirin and plans for further liver evaluation.
